# testdata

- `corpora/`: downloaded Canterbury and Silesia corpora (gitignored), plus
  `SOURCES.json` recording URLs and SHA-256 (P0-08).
- `generated/`: the deterministic conformance corpus generated by
  `crates/oracle` (gitignored, regenerated by `make corpus`/`make corpus-full`,
  i.e. `cargo run --release -p oracle -- generate --tier quick|full`).
- `MANIFEST.json`: committed hash manifest for `generated/` (P1-03). One
  entry per generated file: id, tier (`synthetic`/`canterbury`/`silesia`),
  input source and its SHA-256/length, compression parameters (framing,
  level, strategy, window_bits, mem_level, optional dictionary), and the
  generated file's own path/SHA-256/length. `oracle generate --tier T`
  (no `--write-manifest`) verifies `generated/` against this file, self-
  healing missing files but reporting (not silently overwriting) any file
  present with the wrong hash. `--write-manifest` regenerates and rewrites
  the entries for `T`'s tiers, keeping any other tier's existing entries.
- `malformed/`: hand-built malformed streams and `EXPECTED.tsv` (P2-04).

Paths in this tree use `rfc1951`/`rfc1950`/`rfc1952` to name the three
framings, never the names of existing implementations (CLAUDE.md C11).
